everything in the Constitution is ratified). Hand-written rather than generated, because §31.4's STATUS

description: A partner-tier structure belongs in Partner, Reseller and Distribution arrangements, and never in an end-customer agreement.

source_document: Legal Constitution, Lawyer Review Version L1.10 — docs/02-legal-domain/LEGAL_CONSTITUTION_L1.10.md
source_quote: Partner tiers such as Silver, Gold, Diamond, and Platinum are applicable only to Partner, Reseller, and Distribution arrangements. They are NOT applicable to normal/end customers. A normal/end customer agreement (e.g. a standard MSA) is not expected to contain, and should not be evaluated against, a tier-based discount/commission structure of this kind.

constitution.topic: Section 31.4 — Partner / Reseller / Distribution Tier Structure

evaluation_rules._note: presence is established by the mapping layer alone (45D)

_calibration: NO THRESHOLD AND NO PERCENTAGE IS CARRIED, DELIBERATELY. §31.4's STATUS ratifies the APPLICABILITY ('Partner/Reseller/Distribution only, not end customers': Company-approved, stakeholder-confirmed) and expressly does NOT confirm the figures: 'Specific thresholds/percentages: historical evidence only, not confirmed as current commercial values.' The section also records a live contradiction — [Partner A] states Rs. 60,000 as a MONTHLY threshold while [Partner B]'s only numeric reference calls it ANNUAL — so a numeric standard here would have to pick one, which is rule 7's failure mode. PRESENCE checks that a tier structure is ADDRESSED; a human reads the numbers.

`not_applicable_to` carries §31.4's own exclusion ('NOT applicable to MSA, NDA, SLA, or other normal/end-customer agreements'), so an end-customer agreement is never flagged for lacking a tier structure — the Constitution states that absence is 'correct, not a deviation'.
Appendix B has no clause category for partner tiering, so `constitution.topic` takes §31.4's own heading. A routing label, not a position.
